Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The same Apocalypse build, reached later and along a different road. The base build has a hard structural problem its own guide states plainly: it cannot be played before level 32, because Umbral Chains' Chain Whips upgrade is what builds Apocalypse stacks fast enough to circumvent the Ultimate's cooldown, so the published levelling route runs a Lunatic shell - Command Fallen, Bombardment, Nether Step, Rampage - and respecs at 32 into a build that is then poor until its uniques arrive. This variant keeps the Lunatic shell all the way through the early endgame and respecs only when the gear that makes Apocalypse good is actually equipped. There is a second reason, and it is a genuine source disagreement rather than a preference: InfinityBuilds' 2026-08-02 list rates a Command Fallen Warlock S tier and its author calls it 'the smoothest Warlock build to play in Season 14 and a strong contender for Tower leaderboards', while Maxroll has no Warlock build above B on its endgame list and the 3.1.2 class snapshot ranks the class dead last. This repo does not resolve that in InfinityBuilds' favour - one list is not evidence against three - but a hybrid that spends longer in the Command Fallen shell is a cheap way to hedge it. The base build remains rank 1 for the class.

Rotation
  1. Umbral Chains to stack, Annihilation as a rhythm rather than an Ultimate, Dark Prison for Fortify and Weaken, Bombardment and Rampage to fill.
  2. Command Valloch for Overpower.
Variants

Leveling — Command Fallen to keep demons out, Umbral Chains to group, Bombardment on the pack, Nether Step to reposition. Apocalypse when it happens to be up rather than as a plan.
Move on when Level 70 and Torment 1. Note what is *not* a trigger here: level 32. The base build respecs there and this one does not.

Early Endgame — Command Fallen on cooldown, Umbral Chains to pull, Bombardment on the pack, Rampage to move. Undying Aspect on the boots is what makes the Scorching Fragment swap survivable later - get it imprinted before you make that swap, not after.
Move on when Fleshwrit Carapace and Hands of the Worldbreaker both equipped. This is the respec point: with the chest giving Apocalypse the Sigil tag, the Ultimate starts feeding the Rite of the Nameless charm set itself, and only then is the Apocalypse tree better than the shell you have been running.

Late Endgame — The base build's loop: Umbral Chains to stack, Annihilation as a rhythm rather than an Ultimate, Dark Prison for Fortify and Weaken, Bombardment and Rampage to fill. Keyword sources, from the base guide's table: Vulnerable from Aspect of Accursed Touch, Fortify and Weaken from Dark Prison, Hex from Sigil of Subversion, Overpower from Command Valloch, Barrier from the Que rune, Volatility from Scorching Fragment and Sigil of Chaos.
Move on when Moloch's Beating Flame and Ring of Starless Skies equipped, and the paragon board past 250.

Pushing — Unchanged from the base build. Worth restating the staleness warning that applies to both pages: the guide behind them was last updated 2026-06-30 on patch 3.1.0 and has not been revised for 3.1.1 or 3.1.2, so treat its numbers as the oldest in this season's build set.

Lootfilter

Apocalypse Warlock - Maxroll Soft / Medium / Strict (in-guide import codes) — View Filter

maxroll.gg

The base build's own in-guide import codes in three strictness tiers. Use Soft for longer than the base build suggests: this variant spends its early endgame in a Lunatic shell that wants Wrath Regeneration and demon-adjacent rolls the Apocalypse-tuned Strict tier will hide. Switch tiers when you respec, not before.

Uniques
  • gloves Warlock class unique. Dedicated table: Grigoire, The Galvanic Saint, in the Hall of the Penitent south of Ked Bardu, Dry Steppes; 1x Lair Key, key from Helltide. Where →
  • chest Warlock class unique, and the item this variant waits for before respeccing - it is what gives Apocalypse the Sigil tag so the Ultimate feeds the Rite of the Nameless charm set itself. Dedicated table: Lord Zir, in The Darkened Way east of Kyovashad, Fractured Peaks; 1x Lair Key, key from the Blood Maiden in Helltide. Where →
  • amulet Warlock class unique, buffed in 3.1.x from 8-11% to 20-30%. Dedicated table: The Butcher, in Gea Kul, Kehjistan; 1x Greater Lair Key from the Initiate lair bosses. He is also summonable as a Pit Guardian through the Pit Butcher War Plan node, which is the cheaper route once your War Plans are up. Where →
  • ring 1 Mythic Unique. Rare drop from any lair boss or a Horadric Cube craft with Pandemonium Fragments; only one Cube-crafted Mythic may be equipped at a time. Where →
  • weapon Mythic Unique two-handed sword, legal for Warlock. General Mythic pool from any lair boss that drops Mythics, or a Horadric Cube craft. Where →

Point allocation, in order112 points across 41 nodes

Recorded from the guide's own Maxroll planner profile, not from the guide page -- the page renders its tree from the planner and carries no node text at all. Points are the profile's own allocation; skills rank to 15 and most upgrade mods to 3. This stage records the separate Apocalypse Warlock Levelling Guide's own planner profile.

Skill point priority

How to run them

The guide switches the hire once, at the levelling-to-endgame line. While levelling it hires Varyana 'for more healing and Vulnerable uptime', taking Taste of Flesh for the healing and Hysteria for attack speed. From the Starter variant onward - and identically across Starter, Midgame, Endgame and Tower Push - it hires Raheir 'for more survivability and Inspiration', which is the tree recorded above. The Reinforcement never changes at any stage: Aldkin, 'for damage reduction from Field of Languish'. Read the whole slot as damage control rather than damage: it is spent entirely on the cons box's 'mediocre survivability' and on the Scorching Fragment self-burn.

Plan

Said plainly: this guide publishes a War Plans section containing six embedded widgets and not one word of prose - no node names, no priorities, no explanation. The picks below are decoded from the guide's own planner payload, where the allocation is byte-identical across all six profiles from levelling through Tower Push, so there is no stage-by-stage progression to describe either. That makes these the author's real board but leaves them unexplained; the notes here say what each node is for from the general War Plans reference, and nothing has been invented about why this build in particular wants them.

What is lit9 picks recorded on 5 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.
Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The same Apocalypse build, reached later and along a different road. The base build has a hard structural problem its own guide states plainly: it cannot be played before level 32, because Umbral Chains' Chain Whips upgrade is what builds Apocalypse stacks fast enough to circumvent the Ultimate's cooldown, so the published levelling route runs a Lunatic shell - Command Fallen, Bombardment, Nether Step, Rampage - and respecs at 32 into a build that is then poor until its uniques arrive. This variant keeps the Lunatic shell all the way through the early endgame and respecs only when the gear that makes Apocalypse good is actually equipped. There is a second reason, and it is a genuine source disagreement rather than a preference: InfinityBuilds' 2026-08-02 list rates a Command Fallen Warlock S tier and its author calls it 'the smoothest Warlock build to play in Season 14 and a strong contender for Tower leaderboards', while Maxroll has no Warlock build above B on its endgame list and the 3.1.2 class snapshot ranks the class dead last. This repo does not resolve that in InfinityBuilds' favour - one list is not evidence against three - but a hybrid that spends longer in the Command Fallen shell is a cheap way to hedge it. The base build remains rank 1 for the class.

Rotation
  1. Umbral Chains to stack, Annihilation as a rhythm rather than an Ultimate, Dark Prison for Fortify and Weaken, Bombardment and Rampage to fill.
  2. Command Valloch for Overpower.
Variants

Leveling — Command Fallen to keep demons out, Umbral Chains to group, Bombardment on the pack, Nether Step to reposition. Apocalypse when it happens to be up rather than as a plan.
Move on when Level 70 and Torment 1. Note what is *not* a trigger here: level 32. The base build respecs there and this one does not.

Early Endgame — Command Fallen on cooldown, Umbral Chains to pull, Bombardment on the pack, Rampage to move. Undying Aspect on the boots is what makes the Scorching Fragment swap survivable later - get it imprinted before you make that swap, not after.
Move on when Fleshwrit Carapace and Hands of the Worldbreaker both equipped. This is the respec point: with the chest giving Apocalypse the Sigil tag, the Ultimate starts feeding the Rite of the Nameless charm set itself, and only then is the Apocalypse tree better than the shell you have been running.

Late Endgame — The base build's loop: Umbral Chains to stack, Annihilation as a rhythm rather than an Ultimate, Dark Prison for Fortify and Weaken, Bombardment and Rampage to fill. Keyword sources, from the base guide's table: Vulnerable from Aspect of Accursed Touch, Fortify and Weaken from Dark Prison, Hex from Sigil of Subversion, Overpower from Command Valloch, Barrier from the Que rune, Volatility from Scorching Fragment and Sigil of Chaos.
Move on when Moloch's Beating Flame and Ring of Starless Skies equipped, and the paragon board past 250.

Pushing — Unchanged from the base build. Worth restating the staleness warning that applies to both pages: the guide behind them was last updated 2026-06-30 on patch 3.1.0 and has not been revised for 3.1.1 or 3.1.2, so treat its numbers as the oldest in this season's build set.

Reasoning

Based onApocalypse Warlock
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. The level-32 respec is deferred. The base build's own levelling guide runs a Lunatic shell to 32 and then switches; this variant keeps Command Fallen, Bombardment and Rampage on the bar through the early endgame and switches only at the late endgame, when Fleshwrit Carapace and Hands of the Worldbreaker are actually equipped. Nothing is lost structurally: the skill tree for the early endgame is the levelling allocation, carried forward rather than rewritten.
  2. Rampage with Demonic Smash replaces Nether Step from the early endgame rather than waiting for the Anathema of the Primes charm. The base guide credits that charm with buying the swap; this variant makes the swap on the shell it is already running and treats the charm as an upgrade rather than a gate.
  3. Twisted Fragment is kept as the shard until a healing source is actually online. The base guide opens its equipment section requiring one, because Scorching Fragment burns you when you attack; it names Twisted Fragment as the levelling fallback and this variant simply holds it longer.
  4. Undying Aspect is prioritised onto boots early rather than transfigured onto the amulet later - the same healing requirement, solved with the cheaper of the guide's own three options (boots imprint, amulet transfiguration, or a large Life on Hit weapon roll).
  5. Wrath Regeneration leads the boots and ring priorities through the early stages, because a Command Fallen shell spends Wrath continuously where the Apocalypse loop spends it in bursts.
  6. War Plans are inherited from the base build's planner payload unchanged - the allocation is byte-identical across all six of its profiles, so there is nothing variant-specific to change - with only the summary re-worded.

Provoke

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 25 seconds

Raheir Taunts enemies around you for 5 seconds. You gain 5% Damage Reduction for each target, up to 20%.

Ground Slam

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Round Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Strike

Raheir brutalizes the ground, dealing 160% Physical damage and Slowing enemies by 30% for 6 seconds. Targets in the center of the slam are Slowed by 60% instead.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir swings a round shield at enemies, dealing 85% Physical damage. Every 20 swings, Raheir Heals you for 8% of your Maximum Life.

Shield Charge

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Tower Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Bash

Raheir rushes forward aggressively, dealing 110% Physical damage and Taunting nearby enemies for 4 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir bashes enemies with a tower shield, dealing 80% Physical damage and Fortifying you for 0.2% of your Maximum Life.

Crater

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Raheir strikes the ground 3 times, each burst dealing 30% Physical damage and Pulling In enemies. The final burst deals 40% more Physical damage and additionally Stuns enemies for 2 seconds.

Raheir's Guard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir grants you 15%[+] Armor.

Vanguard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir Slows surrounding enemies by 40%.

Mocking Lure

PassiveRaheir

You deal 15%[x] increased damage to enemies Taunted by Raheir.

Iron Wolf's Ward

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he Knocks Back Close enemies and Taunts Distant enemies for 4 seconds.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Iron Wolf's Call

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, your next 4 Core Skills within 10 seconds deal 25%[x] increased damage and cost no Resource.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 25%.

Sundering Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's final Crater burst deals 200%[x] increased damage and inflicts Vulnerable on enemies for 4 seconds.

Shield Throw

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Raheir throws his shield, dealing 450% Physical damage and Taunting enemies for 5 seconds. The shield bounces up to 9 times and cannot bounce to the same target twice.

Iron Wolf's Arrival

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he also casts Ground Slam and Shield Throw.

Raheir's Valiance's Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Consecrated Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's Shield Throw Consecrates enemies for 6 seconds. Directly damaging a Consecrated enemy Heals you for 6% of your Maximum Life, once per target.

Bastion

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 30 seconds

Raheir takes a protective position for 5 seconds, redirecting 90% of the damage that would be dealt to surrounding allies to himself for 5 seconds.

Bastion's initial cast also grants surrounding allies Unstoppable for 1.0 seconds.

Iron Wolf's Virtue

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he Heals you for 25% of your Maximum Life.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Inspiration

PassiveRaheir

Enemies affected by Raheir's Ground Slam take 15%[x] increased damage.

Allies affected by Raheir's Bastion deal 25%[x] increased damage.

Raheir's Aegis

PassiveRaheir

Raheir grants you 15% Resistance to All Elements.

Draw Fire

PassiveRaheir

When you use a Healing Potion, Raheir Taunts enemies around him for 4 seconds. Can only occur once every 20 seconds.

Tree of Plenty

Tree of Whispers

The Tree offers a fourth Whisper Cache choice.

Headrotten Feast

Tree of Whispers

Headrotten Bosses that are drawn to Exposed Roots have +1 Monster Power, and will always drop a Whisper Cache.

Resplendent Favor

Tree of Whispers

Each Whisper Cache has a chance to drop a Resplendent Spark.

Malignant Invasion

Tree of Whispers

Varshan can now appear in a Whisper Ambushes.

Slay Varshan to earn the contents of an Ancestral Collection of Chaos .

Grim Retribution

Tree of Whispers

Completing a Whisper has a chance to trigger a Whisper Ambush.

These enemies have a chance to burst out the contents of a Collection of Chaos when slain.

Roots of Power

Tree of Whispers

Enemies that are drawn to Exposed Roots have +1 Monster Power.

Planting Corrupted Roots in Helltides yields double rewards.

Colossal Foe

Tree of Whispers

Whisper Ambushes sometimes include Bosses.

These Bosses will always burst out the contents of a Greater Collection of Chaos when slain.

Simple Gifts

Tree of Whispers

The Tree only offers one Whisper Cache choice that will always be a Material Collection or a Collection of Chaos.

Corrupted Roots

Tree of Whispers

Whisper Caches sometimes contain Corrupted Roots.

Plant Corrupted Roots to grow an Exposed Root. These will attract nearby enemies, and have a chance to grow larger and summon more fearsome enemies.

The regions of Sanctuary each bear different fruit.

Wisdom of Whispers

Tree of Whispers

Gain 50% more Experience Orbs in Whisper Caches.

Fortune or Famine

Tree of Whispers

Whisper Caches from the Tree of Whispers are always at least of Greater Quality... or Junk.

Material Wealth

Tree of Whispers

The Tree now only offers Material Collections.

Grim Mysteries

Tree of Whispers

Collections of Chaos are replaced with Collections of Mysteries.

These caches can drop anything.

Chaotic Favor

Tree of Whispers

Completing a Whisper has a small chance to award a Collection of Chaos.

Branching Pathways

Nightmare Dungeons

When advancing to the next dungeon in a Nightmare Escalation, 2 additional Horadric Portals appear.

Fearless Conviction

Nightmare Dungeons

While in a Nightmare Dungeon, killing Elites and Champions grants you stacks of Conviction.

Getting hit by an Elite or Champion causes you to lose a stack of Conviction.

A Conviction Chest appears at the end of the dungeon that grants rewards for each remaining Conviction. This chest has a higher than normal chance to award Attuned Primordial Dust.

Goblinfall

Nightmare Dungeons

Treasure Goblins have a small chance to drop a Nightmare Sigil with the Treasure Breach affix.

Nemesis

Nightmare Dungeons

Activating a Shrine in a Nightmare Dungeon causes up to 7 Elites to ambush you.

Gauntlet

Nightmare Dungeons

While in a Nightmare Dungeon, slaying an enemy while empowered by a Shrine traps their soul within you.

When the Shrine buff expires, all trapped souls escape and spawn around you as renewed enemies.

Souls will be lost when moving between dungeons in an Escalation Dungeon.

Horadric Hunter

Nightmare Dungeons

Kill 25 Elites across Nightmare Dungeons to reveal a Horadric Altar. Activating it results in one of the following outcomes:

Summon Elites

Summon Treasure Goblins

Summon The Butcher

Gain Riches

Terrible Misfortune

Altar of Avarice

Nightmare Dungeons

Horadric Altars are replaced with Goblin Altars that only summon Treasure Goblins.

Cipher Maps

Nightmare Dungeons

Whenever you would reveal a Horadric Altar, you reveal 2 instead.

Rewarded Faith

Nightmare Dungeons

Gain a random additional buff when claiming a Shrine in a Nightmare Dungeon.

Greed is Good

Nightmare Dungeons

Killing a Treasure Goblin in a Nightmare Dungeon has a small chance to spawn a portal that takes you to the Goblin's Retreat.

Waking Spoils

Nightmare Dungeons

After completing a Nightmare Dungeon, a War's Bounty Chest will spawn that grants additional rewards.

Recurring Nightmare

Nightmare Dungeons

Bosses in Nightmare Dungeons gain +1 Monster Power and have a chance to drop an Escalation Sigil when slain.

Escalation Sigils can only appear in Torment+ difficulty.

Dread Revival

Nightmare Dungeons

Bosses in Nightmare Dungeons have a chance to revive when slain.

Night Terrors

Helltide

You have a chance to be ambushed by Hellborne in Nightmare Dungeons.

Hellborne have a small chance to drop a Profane Mindcage when slain.

Hell's Prize

Helltide

Hell's Prize chests will now appear in Helltide.

These chests offer a massive torrent of items for 666 Aberrant Cinders.

Fall of the Fell

Helltide

Harbingers will emerge from falling meteors twice as often, and drop twice as many Aberrant Cinders when slain.

Harbingers in Helltide have +1 Monster Power.

Meat Brothers

Helltide

Instead of Hellborne, two Butchers that are connected with flaming chains ambush you.

These Butchers each have a high chance to drop a Profane Mindcage when slain.

Hellmouth

Helltide

When a Hellwyrm emerges, it unleashes one of the following:

A Chaos Rift, which releases varied rewards upon collapse.

Maggots, which burst out Experience Orbs when slain.

Bloodseekers, which are more likely to drop Ancestral items when slain.

Wretched Vermin

Helltide

Demonic Rats will frequently attack you in Helltide.

Ashes to Ashes

Helltide

On death, lose all your Aberrant Cinders.

For every 100 Aberrant Cinders you pick up, you gain an additional 10.

Undying Embers

Helltide

You lose no Aberrant Cinders on death.

Infernal Rite

Helltide

Ambushes spawn up to four additional Hellborne.

Hellborne have a higher chance to drop Unique items when slain.

Planar Tremors

Helltide

Hellwyrms will always open a Chaos Rift, and enemies that emerge from it gain +1 Monster Power.

The first time a Chaos Rift opens, there is a chance that another will open.

Tainted Shrines

Helltide

While empowered by a Shrine in Helltide, slain enemies grant double the progress to your Threat Level.

Hated Foe

Helltide

Maximum Threat enemies that ambush you gain +1 Monster Power.

Chaotic Echoes

Helltide

Collapsed Chaos Rifts have a chance to reopen.

Bursting Brood

Helltide

Maggots and Pangs of Duriel explode when killed and will often drop Boss Trophies.

Writhe and Rot

Helltide

Hellwyrms will always spew Maggots that gain +1 Monster Power.

Sometimes, a Pang of Duriel will also crawl forth. Lair Keys often burst out of Pangs of Duriel.

Bound by Blood

Helltide

Bloodseekers are connected with flaming chains.

When slain, Bloodseekers drop items that match the category of the last opened Tortured Gift.

Crimson Scent

Helltide

Hellwyrms will always call forth Bloodseekers that gain +1 Monster Power.

Greater Bloodseekers may also emerge, which have a high chance to drop Legendary items when slain.

Idols of War

The Undercity

Greater Tributes of Armament more frequently drop throughout Sanctuary and have an additional Bargain choices.

Trials and Tributes

The Undercity

For each Portal Prankster you slay within the Undercity, a Tribute Chest appears after killing the District Boss.

Tribute Chests are unlocked by offering a Tribute.

Gutter Filth

The Undercity

When you activate any Beacon within the Undercity, there is a small chance to summon a Portal Prankster.

Invasion Portals will sometimes summon Rats of varying amounts.

Endless Swarm

The Undercity

Invasion Portals now appear in the Undercity.

The enemies that emerge grant Attunement when slain.

Jade Epiphany

The Undercity

When you gain an Attunement level in the Undercity, Experience Orbs appear around you.

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Finely Tuned

The Undercity

Gain additional Tuning Prisms when completing the Undercity at maximum Attunement.

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Pathfinder

The Undercity

When you reach maximum Attunement, a portal to the final floor of the Undercity appears.

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Unfortunate Souls

The Undercity

Invasion Portals can now summon Wisps that attach to you and vanish if you die.

Each Wisp you save will reward you with Forgotten Souls and other Crafting Materials at the end of the run.

Initiative

The Undercity

When you find the District Boss you gain the Initiative buff, which has a duration equal to your remaining Time. Initiative is lost upon death.

If you slay the District Boss with Initiative active, you receive Tribute rewards as if your Attunement was 2 higher (max 6).

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Last Gasp

The Undercity

Time collected from slain enemies with 5 seconds or less remaining in the Undercity doubles the Time earned.

Bauble Day

The Undercity

If you slay a Portal Prankster within the Undercity, the Cabochon Merchant will appear after killing the District Boss.

The Cabochon Merchant will sell you Runes and Gems for Gold.

Lair of Plenty

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses have +1 Monster Power.

Gain +1 Hoard Chest when you slay a Lair Boss (excluding Belial).

Infernal Deception

Lair Bosses

Belial can now ambush you after completing the Infernal Hordes.

Two by Two

Lair Bosses

After opening a Hoard Chest, there is a low chance a Portal will open that will take you to the Nemesis Lair, where you will fight two Initiate Lair Bosses at the same time.

Slaying both will yield great rewards.

You cannot enter a Nemesis Lair from Belial's throne room.

Nemesis Tides

Lair Bosses

Initiate Lair Bosses have a chance to appear instead of Helltide Commanders after Helltide Events.

Killing Lair Bosses in Helltides while earning the Event Mastery grants many random Lair Boss materials.

This only occurs in Torment+ difficulties.

Exotic Armory

Lair Bosses

Hoard Chests drop one additional Unique Item, but it can be for any Class.

Greater Nemesis

Lair Bosses

After completing a Nemesis Lair, there is a chance that a portal will appear that will take you to a Greater Nemesis Lair. Within this heinous place lies two Greater Lair Bosses.

Slaying both bosses will yield great rewards.

Lair of Runes

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses have +1 Monster Power.

Lair Bosses have a higher chances of dropping specific Runes.

Ultimate Nemesis

Lair Bosses

After defeating all Bosses within the Greater Nemesis Lair, the Call Of Evil will appear. This altar will accept 3 Superior Lair Keys and open a Portal that takes you to the Ultimate Nemesis Lair.

Inside the Ultimate Nemesis Lair, all enemies gain +5 Monster Power. Defeating the Boss Encounter will award you with 10 Hoard Chests worth of Items.

Golden Hoard

Lair Bosses

All equipment that would drop from Hoard Chests are converted to Gold, except for Unique and Mythic items.

Grigoire's Gambit

Lair Bosses

After opening a Tortured Gift in Helltides, there is a chance Grigoire's knights will ambush you.

When killed in Helltide, they may drop Unique Items available from his Hoard Chest.

Duriel's Invasion

Lair Bosses

When summoning the Blood Maiden in Helltides, there is a chance Duriel can be summoned instead.

Killing Duriel in Helltides can now drop Unique Items from his Hoard Chest.

Out of the Cold

Lair Bosses

When fighting a Boss in a Nightmare Dungeon, the Beast in Ice has a chance to appear and attack you.

When this occurs, killing the Nightmare Dungeon Boss has a chance to drop Unique Items from the Beast in Ice's Hoard Chest.

Children of Zir

Lair Bosses

When exploring the Pit, Lord Zir's Bloodseekers can now ambush you.

Killing them in the Pit can now drop Unique Items from his Hoard Chest.

Dog of Astaroth

Lair Bosses

When fighting a Boss in a Nightmare Dungeon, the Amalgam of Rage has a chance to appear and attack you.

Killing the Amalgam of Rage in Nightmare Dungeons can drop Unique Items associated with Astaroth

Embers of Anguish

Lair Bosses

When exploring the Pit, Embers of Anguish can appear. Activating one drops Progress Orbs, and causes Andariel to ambush you at the end of the Pit.

Killing Andariel in the Pit can now drop Unique Items from her Hoard Chest.

Blood of Bartuc

Lair Bosses

The Fell Council in the Infernal Hordes has +1 Monster Power.

After defeating the Fell Council, the Spoils of Greater Equipment may drop Unique Items associated with Bartuc.

Varshan's Vengeance

Lair Bosses

Varshan and his minions can now appear in a Chaos Wave within the Infernal Hordes.

After killing Varshan in the Infernal Hordes, the Spoils of Greater Equipment may drop Unique Items available from his Hoard Chest.

Exalted Council

Infernal Hordes

Bartuc and the Fell Council have +1 Monster Power and drop additional items when slain.

Council Coffers

Infernal Hordes

The Chest of Talismans will appear after defeating either the Fell Council or Bartuc.

Infernal Hoard

Infernal Hordes

Defeating either the Fell Council or Bartuc reveals the Hoard of Greater Equipment, which contains a colossal deluge of equipment and other rewards.

Forged in Flame

Infernal Hordes

Obducite drops instead of Gem Fragments in the Infernal Hordes.

Flawless Find

Infernal Hordes

Gem Fragments drop instead of Obducite in the Infernal Hordes.

Method and Madness

Infernal Hordes

Your Infernal Offerings are more likely to share a category with your previous choice.

Impending Doom

Infernal Hordes

When the current wave has 10 seconds remaining, Aether Events spawn at all locations.

The Black Pact

Infernal Hordes

An ominous altar appears between waves in the Infernal Hordes.

It can be invoked only once, and provides an Infernal Offering that shares a category with your previous choice.

Reign in Hell

Infernal Hordes

An additional Infernal Offering appears each wave.

However, you suppress Chaos Waves from appearing.

Total Chaos

Infernal Hordes

Chaos Waves appear more frequently.

However, one less Infernal Offering appears each wave.

Bedlam

Infernal Hordes

When you enter a Chaos Wave, gain +50 Aether and all enemies in the Infernal Hordes gain +1 Monster Power.

Pulse of Aether

Infernal Hordes

Suppressing a Chaos Wave grants +50 Aether.

All enemies in the Infernal Hordes gain +1 Monster Power.

Cult of Annihilation

Infernal Hordes

Doomsayers appear during the Infernal Hordes.

Doomsayers are dangerous enemies but also drop Aether.

Scale of Tathamet

Infernal Hordes

Once per wave the Scale of Tathamet may appear, a primordial relic that kills all enemies within the Infernal Hordes.

Devil's Deal

Infernal Hordes

At the start of the Infernal Hordes, gain an Infernal Challenge.

Completing the Infernal Challenge will grant +200 Aether.

Choron's Haste

The Pit

The Pit gains the Haste Mastery objective.

When you kill the Guardian gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance for every 5 minutes left on the Timer.

Damned Thieves

The Pit

Orb Thieves have a chance to spawn in The Pit.

Orb Thieves drop an immense amount of Progress Orbs when killed, but leave a trail of Traps in their wake.

Heart of Stone

The Pit

Begin The Pit carrying the Heart of Stone, a fragile relic that is dropped after taking sustained damage and breaks after dropping 10 times.

While you carry it, enemies can drop bonus Progress Orbs.

After slaying the Guardian, Choron's Pedestal appears. Deposit the Heart of Stone within to gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance.

Choron's Blessing

The Pit

Gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance for completing The Pit.

Choron's Favor

The Pit

Special events and encounters become more common in higher Difficulty Tiers of The Pit.

Choron's Soul

The Pit

Choron's Soul now spawns with the Awakened Glyphstone.

Choron's Soul will drop 1 Progress Orb per Glyph Upgrade Chance offered.

All Progress Orbs in The Pit now grant Experience.

Choron's Flesh

The Pit

Choron's Flesh now spawns with the Awakened Glyphstone.

Choron's Flesh will allow you to get valuable Equipment by consuming one of your Glyph Upgrade Chances.

Choron's Shortcut

The Pit

Choron's Portal randomly appears in The Pit.

When used, it will send you to the entrance to the next Pit Floor, or become Unstable and summon either an Elite or a Shrine.

Cursed Rituals

The Pit

Different Ritual Sites now spawn in the Pit, and special Materials can spawn in different environments:

Choron's Blood appears in foliage dense regions

Choron's Sweat appears in stony locations

Choron's Tears appears in mystical places

Sacrificing these Materials at Ritual Sites may grant Gold, Materials, Items, and more.

Pit Butcher

The Pit

The Butcher has a chance to appear anywhere in The Pit.

The Butcher is a Guardian and killing him will complete the run.

However, you fail the run if he kills any player.

Cursed Merchant

The Pit

The Cursed Merchant has a chance to appear when completing the Pit.

The Cursed Merchant will sell Equipment for Artificers Stones.

Cursed Offerings

The Pit

Cursed Machines have a chance to appear while exploring the Pit.

Cursed Machines cost Artificers Stones to activate. Activating one will grant you valuable materials and attract vicious enemies.

The more Cursed Machines you find in a single Pit run, the more lucrative the rewards will become.

Choron's Wager

The Pit

Choron's Wager can appear in The Pit.

Activate it with Artificer's Stones to acquire a challenge, which grants a large amount of Artificer's Stones when completed.
